agree.reason: The opening with her own $600K quote and the clear 'sits on top' line could get Dana to take a 20-minute call, but nothing gives her a way past her IT director, so the reader most likely to resist has little reason to change her mind.

honest.reason: Every figure comes from the brief and the result is correctly tied to one customer, though it uses only the strongest result and leaves out the weaker 2.8-to-2.2 customer, so the overall picture looks a little better than it is.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the $75,000 annual cost but never sets it against what a roughly 54% cut in mis-picks could mean for her $600K (about $320K a year), so the one derivation that would favour the writer is missing.

right_comparison.reason: Doing nothing is implied by the $600K quote, but the email never puts that ongoing loss side by side with the $75K price, so the alternative is mentioned and not actually compared.

qualification.reason: The claim rests on one customer, yet the email gives no checkable hedge, such as what reduction she could expect by a given week or what happens if it doesn't arrive, and offers only a vague 'see if this would work.'

objections.reason: Saying it doesn't replace her warehouse system and sits on top of it meets the IT objection in part, but it never says how much IT work the three-week setup takes or whether it touches the warehouse system at all, which is what the IT director will ask.

fit.reason: It's short, broken into lines that read easily on a phone, and has the right form for a cold email with a single clear ask.
